chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Qummī, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام regarding His saying:
“And We had indeed made a covenant with Adam before.”

“Words concerning Muḥammad, and ʿAlī, and Fāṭimah, and al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn, and the Imams عليهم السلام from their offspring; then he forgot. Thus, by Allah, it was revealed to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله.”

key_terms.آدَمَ: Adam, the first prophet and human addressed in the verse.
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: The Imams عليهم السلام from the progeny mentioned in the report.
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّتِهِمْ: Their offspring; indicating descent from those named.
key_terms.عَهِدْنَا: We made a covenant; indicating a divine pledge or binding charge.
key_terms.فَنَسِيَ: Then he forgot; referring to Adam in the cited wording.
key_terms.كَلِمَاتٍ: Words; interpreted here as words concerning specific sacred persons.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدٍ: Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the Messenger of Allah.
key_terms.نَزَلَتْ: It was revealed; affirming this wording as revelation according to the narration.

ai.seo_question: How does this narration interpret Allah’s covenant with Adam in relation to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This narration presents the verse about the covenant with Adam as referring to words concerning Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, and the Imams عليهم السلام from their progeny. It frames the passage as a Quranic commentary highlighting the pre-temporal covenant connected to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and their wilayah.
